ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Flannery O'Connor — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for bladder symptoms on immunosuppression

text.paragraph: Burning on passing urine and going often for two days. [S]

Ms. O'Connor is a 25-year-old writer with systemic lupus erythematosus and class III lupus nephritis, seven weeks into treatment with mycophenolate 1000 mg twice daily, weekly belimumab, hydroxychloroquine, losartan, and prednisone, now 15 mg a day. For two days she has had burning on passing urine, frequency, urgency, and lower abdominal discomfort. She has no fever on her home thermometer, chills, back or flank pain, vomiting, vaginal discharge, or rash, and her joints are quiet. She has a levonorgestrel intrauterine system. She called because she had been told that any infection on her treatment should be seen the same day, and she wanted to know whether this was her kidneys. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1950-06-15; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Pain and swelling of the small joints of both hands, the wrists, and the knees for three months, with an hour of morning stiffness, evening fevers to 38 °C, fatigue, and a red rash over the cheeks and nose after sun; told elsewhere it might be rheumatoid arthritis; cause to be established

S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus at the second visit; joint pain in 1950 with suspected rheumatoid arthritis is documented (D).
Protein and blood in the urine: protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.6 g/g and 18 red cells per high-power field, with normal creatinine; cause to be established
S — Synthetic presenting finding at the index visit, superseded by the kidney biopsy diagnosis at the third visit.

Systemic lupus erythematosus, classified by the EULAR/ACR criteria (ANA 1:640 homogeneous; score 32 before the biopsy): inflammatory arthritis, acute cutaneous lupus (malar rash), fever, leukopenia with lymphopenia, mild thrombocytopenia, low C3 and C4, anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm positive; antiphospholipid antibodies and lupus anticoagulant negative
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis and results; her systemic lupus erythematosus, diagnosed in Atlanta in late 1950 or early 1951, is documented (D), but no finding from her lifetime is used.

Lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS class III (A), focal proliferative, on kidney biopsy: endocapillary proliferation in 9 of 30 glomeruli, activity index 6 of 24, chronicity index 1 of 12, full-house immunofluorescence; no thrombotic microangiopathy; urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.8 g/g; normal kidney function
S — Synthetic biopsy result and class; kidney involvement is documented at the end of her life, but no kidney finding from her lifetime is used.
Long-term glucocorticoid treatment for lupus nephritis, tapering to 5 mg a day or less
S — Synthetic treatment status; the documented steroid harm in her life is the reason the episode keeps glucocorticoids low.
Long-term mycophenolate mofetil, with belimumab, for lupus nephritis; bone and infection protection in place
Levonorgestrel intrauterine system for highly effective contraception during mycophenolate treatment
S — Synthetic contraception, chosen by the patient.

Acute cystitis on mycophenolate, belimumab, and prednisone 15 mg: two days of burning, frequency, and urgency without fever or flank pain; urine culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; resolved with seven days of nitrofurantoin
S — Synthetic common infection in an immunosuppressed young woman; coded without hematuria because the persistent hematuria is from her nephritis.

list.item:
Acute cystitis in an immunosuppressed woman (N30.00). Typical bladder symptoms with leukocyte esterase and nitrite on the dipstick, no fever, and no flank tenderness: cystitis without signs of kidney infection. Prednisone can hide fever, so the threshold to treat and to culture is low. White cell count 7.9, creatinine 0.8 unchanged. Nitrofurantoin is first-line with her normal kidney function; trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is avoided because sulfonamides can provoke lupus flares and drug reactions. [S]
Urine culture sent before the first dose.
Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily with food for seven days, a longer course because she is immunosuppressed.
Same-day call for fever, chills, flank pain, or vomiting, which would need assessment for kidney infection.
Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio and sediment not measured today, since infection distorts both; they will be repeated at the three-month visit after the infection clears.

Lupus nephritis on treatment (M32.14). No sign of a flare: joints quiet, no rash, creatinine stable. Potassium 4.6, normal, is the first potassium since losartan was started. [S]
Continue mycophenolate, belimumab, hydroxychloroquine, losartan, and the prednisone taper without change.
Basic metabolic panel added to the standing blood count orders.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update. Ann Rheum Dis 2024;83(1):15-29 (2023); 2024 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Guideline for the Screening, Treatment, and Management of Lupus Nephritis. Arthritis Rheumatol 2025;77(9):1115-1135 (2024); International Clinical Practice Guidelines for the Treatment of Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis and Pyelonephritis in Women: A 2010 Update by the IDSA and ESCMID. Clin Infect Dis 2011;52(5):e103-e120 (2010)

Follow-up: Culture result by telephone in two days. Rheumatology blood count as scheduled. Three-month review in six weeks. Next scheduled visit 1950-07-27: three-month response assessment for lupus nephritis and glucocorticoid taper. [S]
